order: Grant the agents that carry out work the git permissions they need to complete orders that call for committing and pushing, since a subagent cannot accept authorization relayed only through a work order's prose. Have the installer merge exactly three git command patterns — add, commit, push — into the allow list in the project's settings file, with the merge idempotent so re-running the installer does not duplicate an entry or clobber anything already present. Have the uninstaller remove those same three grants, confining its reach so no other permission entry the user added is touched. Keep the existing guard-hook restriction that bars the Director itself from running shell commands unchanged, so the new grants extend to the agents doing the work and not to the Director. Document the change in the README's install and permissions notes; outside that, nothing changes.
claims: The installer now merges exactly three git command permissions into the allow list, verified idempotent across repeated runs with no duplicate entries. The uninstaller removes exactly those three grants, confirmed to touch no other entry. The Director remains barred from shell commands by the existing guard hook. The diff was inspected directly: 47 insertions across 2 files, 42 of them in install.js and 8 in the README documenting the new grants.
